title: Phacoemulsification after trabeculectomy in uveitis associated with Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease: intermediate-term visual outcome, IOP control and trabeculectomy survival

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License)

indication: uveitic glaucoma associated with Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease after a single mitomycin C-enhanced trabeculectomy, IOP controlled with or without medication, phakic eyes, uveitis quiescent for at least 3 months; young adults (retrospective matched comparative study)

groups.description: the article's 'study group': phacoemulsification with in-the-bag foldable IOL through a temporal corneal incision (synechiolysis or iris hooks when needed) in eyes with a prior MMC trabeculectomy; intensive topical and systemic anti-inflammatory treatment afterwards

the article's 'control group': matched eyes with a prior MMC trabeculectomy that did not undergo cataract surgery; follow-up counted from a matched study-entry time (declared for documentation; no series extracted)

exclusions.what: control group IOP series (Table 2 column C3)
exclusions.reason: eyes without a procedure at the reference time: follow-up starts at a matched study-entry time years after trabeculectomy, so there is no preoperative reference of an operated eye (protocol inclusion 1-2); declared as a group for documentation only
final visit without a stated time
reference of the earlier trabeculectomy, not of the phacoemulsification; follow-up times are not counted from the trabeculectomy

exclusions.what: Table 3, Table 4 and Fig. 1 (success status, repeat surgery, Kaplan-Meier trabeculectomy survival)
exclusions.reason: success proportions, counts and Kaplan-Meier estimates are not admissible

exclusions.what: Table 2 medication, LogMAR and BCVA rows
exclusions.reason: not IOP; medication counts are notes only

notes: Role: phacoemulsification is a standard procedure without an investigational agent, so the article's 'study group' is recorded with role control.

Reference kind: baseline IOP before phacoemulsification on the usual regimen (inclusion: IOP controlled with or without antiglaucoma medications; mean number of medications at baseline is tabulated in Table 2 R4 and many eyes used none); no washout is described.
Method: the article does not name a tonometer.
Some eyes needed additional glaucoma surgery during follow-up (Table 4); the article does not state that they were removed from later visit means.

series.notes: mean (±SD) (footnote); per-visit number of eyes in Table 2 'No. of eyes' rows R18, R28, R38, R48 (decreasing with follow-up length: ordinary attrition, no outcome-defined exclusion stated)
